subject: Mathematics

source.topic: Patterns, functions and algebra: Geometric and number patterns
source.subtopic: Number patterns: copy, extend and describe to 150 (multiples of 10, 5, 2, 3, 4); create own number patterns

show.line: A number pattern has a rule. Three, six, nine, twelve. Each number is three more. The rule is add three!

rounds.prompt: Three, six, nine, twelve. What comes next?
Four, eight, twelve, sixteen. What comes next?
Count in tens from a hundred. One hundred and ten, one hundred and twenty. What comes next?
Five, ten, fifteen, twenty. What is the rule of this pattern?
The pattern goes backwards. Fifty, forty-five, forty. What comes next?
rounds.praise: Thirty-five! Take away five each time.

rounds.prompt: Two, four, six, eight, ten. Say the missing number after ten.
Which number is missing? Thirty, forty, gap, sixty.

hints: Find the jump. How much more is each number than the one before?
Say the pattern out loud and keep the same jump.

beat_the_tutor.setup: My turn! Six, nine, twelve. I will say what comes next.
beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! The jump is three. Twelve and three is fifteen.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's add three together. Twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen. Fifteen!

parent_line: Can continue a number pattern and say its rule.
